title: Bitwise Operators
instructions: Deep down, numbers are stored as bits: 1s and 0s. Bitwise operators work on those bits directly.
- <<  shift left  (each shift left doubles the number)
- >>  shift right (each shift right halves it)
You won't use these every day, but they're vital for low-level work, flags, and squeezing out speed.
Example: 6 is 110 in bits and 3 is 011, so 6 & 3 (bits that are 1 in BOTH) is 010, which is 2.
task: Add the line that prints a shifted left by 1, so the output ends with:  a << 1 = 12
